subsystems.name: Ion trap
subsystems.role: holds a string of ions in place using electric fields, with no physical contact.
parts: microfabricated surface trap (gold or aluminium electrodes on silicon)
radio-frequency electrodes that create the confining pseudopotential
segmented DC electrodes for fine positioning
shuttling zones in a QCCD layout

subsystems.name: Ion source and loading
subsystems.role: supplies fresh ions of a chosen isotope.
parts: heated metal oven or laser-ablation target

subsystems.name: Laser and optical system
subsystems.role: cools the ions and drives every logic gate and readout step.
parts: narrow-linewidth stabilised lasers (Doppler and sideband cooling, gates, repump)

subsystems.name: Vacuum and cryogenic enclosure
subsystems.role: keeps ions isolated from background gas for hours.
parts: cryostat cooling the trap to a few kelvin

subsystems.name: Readout optics
subsystems.role: detects each ion's state by the light it scatters.

subsystems.name: Classical control stack
subsystems.role: sequences thousands of precisely timed pulses and corrects drift.

buildSteps.title: Design the trap geometry
buildSteps.detail: Electrode widths and RF frequencies are modelled so the potential well is deep enough to hold a stable ion chain with the desired spacing.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the trap chip
buildSteps.detail: Gold electrodes are patterned on a silicon substrate by photolithography and metal deposition, then diced and wire-bonded to a carrier. The centre-to-centre electrode pitch is typically 100–250 µm.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the vacuum system
buildSteps.detail: The chip is mounted in a vacuum chamber, often on a cold finger, and the whole assembly is baked to remove water and hydrocarbons until the pressure falls to ultra-high vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Load and cool ions
buildSteps.detail: A small oven or ablation target releases neutral atoms, lasers photoionise them, and the resulting ions are Doppler-cooled until they form a stationary chain.

buildSteps.title: Ground-state cooling and characterisation
buildSteps.detail: Sideband cooling brings the shared motional modes near their quantum ground state, and the trap frequencies and stray fields are measured and compensated.

buildSteps.title: Build the optical and electronic drive
buildSteps.detail: Lasers are locked to atomic or cavity references, routed through modulators, and aligned so each ion sees the correct beam; RF and DC lines are calibrated for low phase noise.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the gates
buildSteps.detail: Pulse phases, durations and detunings are tuned, then gate quality is measured with randomised benchmarking and tomography.

buildSteps.title: Scale out
buildSteps.detail: For larger machines, ions are shuttled between trap zones or entangled across modules via photonic links, with each module built and tested as above.

prerequisites.why: surface-electrode chips give reproducible, scalable electrode geometries rather than hand-assembled wire traps.
gate and cooling transitions need linewidths far below the qubit splitting, held stable for hours.
collisions with background gas and thermally driven electrode noise both destroy coherence.
noise on the trapping fields heats the motional modes that gates depend on.
linking separate traps by entanglement is needed to grow beyond what one ion chain can hold.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum error correction at useful scale
prerequisites.why: logical qubits have been demonstrated but not enough of them to run long algorithms.

pathway.milestone: commercial trapped-ion systems with all-to-all connectivity inside one chain and two-qubit fidelities above 99.9%
pathway.unlocks: high-fidelity circuits and early error-corrected logical qubits.

pathway.milestone: many-zone QCCD machines that shuttle ions between memory, gate and readout regions
pathway.unlocks: hundreds of physical qubits with low crosstalk.

pathway.milestone: entanglement between separate modules through photonic links
pathway.unlocks: modular scaling beyond a single trap chip.

pathway.milestone: thousands of logical qubits with real-time decoding
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant computation for chemistry and materials simulation.
